[center][size=6][b][color=#e8a317]★ BIG UPDATE: WHAT'S NEW IN 0.7.7 ★[/color][/b][/size]
[size=4][b]A Barns tab with many pairs per barn  •  Low preset: 7x less hut time than 0.3.1  •  far fewer path searches while riding  •  Quick pair like Quick assign[/b][/size][/center]

[b]Why this update matters:[/b] since 0.5.5 the mod grew a whole new tab and a performance toolbox. You can now manage every [b]Pokémon Barn[/b] from the same window, run several breeding pairs in one barn, and switch the whole mod to a [b]Low[/b] preset that takes the hut code down to a fraction of its old cost. Riding your horse across a big farm used to make the game stutter every few seconds. The mod now postpones and spreads its own work while you ride: the path searches that caused it dropped from about 10-12 per second to about 1. Some hitches remain (see the honest note and the Content Patcher note below). All numbers come straight from the SMAPI logs of the same save. Pelipper Town is still not changed or redistributed.

[size=4][b][color=#e8a317]Highlights[/color][/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Barns tab:[/b] every barn in range with position, distance, pairs used, slots used and short drop chips (M, FQ...). Click a row to open its pair slots.[/*]
[*][b]Manage pairs per barn:[/b] a barn of 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 slots holds 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 pairs. Assign, Breed on/off and Unassign work per pair, per barn or for every ticked barn.[/*]
[*][b]Clear pair rows (new in 0.7.7):[/b] a blue male symbol and a pink female symbol sit right after each Pokémon's name and drop chip, so you see who is who at a glance. The old "Mother / Father" caption is gone, and it no longer overlaps the next row.[/*]
[*][b]Quick pair:[/b] works like Quick assign. Tick the barns, press the button (a green tick appears and the list is NOT filtered), choose the drop chips, press again. Compatible free Pokémon are paired for every free slot.[/*]
[*][b]Name your barns:[/b] press [i]Name[/i] on a row, type a name, OK. The name shows in the list, is searchable and is saved in config.json.[/*]
[*][b]Clear egg warning:[/b] a pair that still holds an egg cannot be unassigned. The window and the log now say "collect the eggs of this pair first".[/*]
[*][b]Performance presets:[/b] a Low / Normal switch and separate switches for hut animations, barn animations, effects, toy play, strolls and markers. Pokémon can teleport on work trips instead of walking, and a frame budget keeps the hut update short.[/*]
[*][b]Riding guard:[/b] while you are mounted, chest batches and path searches are postponed, and workers update less often (off-screen ones the least). A real-time search budget (ms per second) stops one slow search from repeating.[/*]
[*][b]Spike log:[/b] any game update slower than 40 ms is written to the SMAPI log with what ran in it, so lag can be traced instead of guessed.[/*]
[/list]

[i]How this was measured: the built-in [font=Courier New]pe_profile[/font], read from the SMAPI log of each version, on the same save (about 58 working Pokémon, many huts and barns, around 50 mods, SMAPI 4.x, Stardew Valley 1.6). Medians are over the 10-second windows. The two 0.7.x columns are two separate sessions with the Low preset; the hut code has not changed between them. The riding column is a session where the log shows the player mounted. FPS was not recorded in these sessions, so there is no FPS row. The sessions were played at different times of day and with a growing farm, so read this as a real-world comparison, not a lab benchmark. Your numbers will differ.[/i]

[size=3][b]Honest note:[/b] the total hut time fell about seven times against 0.3.1 and about four times against 0.5.5, and the number of path searches fell from 60 to about 3 per second (about 1 per second when riding). But the worst single hut update is [b]higher[/b] than in 0.5.5: about 26 ms on foot and about 80 ms while riding, against 15.5 ms. It is always the same call: Pelipper Town's own "can this Pokémon reach that spot" search. The mod now removes most of the cheap searches, so the ones that remain are the long ones. A search costs about 22 ms when you ride, because each standing check is about three times slower while mounted (0.114 ms against 0.035 ms). This search lives inside Pelipper Town, so this mod can run it less often but cannot make one run shorter.[/size]

[i]The 0.7.2 column comes from the SMAPI log of that version while riding. Everything the mod can postpone while you ride (chest batches, path searches, worker updates) is postponed; you can tune it with [font=Courier New]MountedThrottle[/font], [font=Courier New]MountedSliceTicks[/font], [font=Courier New]MountedOffscreenSliceTicks[/font] and [font=Courier New]MountedSearchMsPerSec[/font]. If you still feel a hitch every second or so while riding, lower [font=Courier New]MountedSearchMsPerSec[/font] (for example to 10): searches then run less often and Pokémon take new jobs a little later while you ride.[/i]

[size=4][b][color=#e8a317]Not this mod: Content Patcher hitches[/color][/b][/size]

The spike log found a second source of lag that has nothing to do with Pokémon. In the riding session there were 25 slow updates between 40 ms and 1 second, and 17 of them came right after Content Patcher reloaded the [font=Courier New]Characters/Dialogue[/font] files of big content packs (Stardew Valley Expanded and a smaller NPC pack in my test save). They repeat every 438 ticks, which is exactly 10 in-game minutes, and each one costs 40-140 ms, on foot and on horseback alike. The same pattern appears in the older 0.5.5 and 0.3.1 logs (88 dialogue reloads in each), so it was never caused by the huts. If you see a hitch every 10 in-game minutes, check your Content Patcher packs first. The spike log line names what ran in that update, so you can tell the two apart.

[size=5][b][color=#e8a317]Description[/color][/b][/size]

[b]Pelipper Expander PokeManager[/b] is a companion mod for [b]Pelipper Town[/b]. It adds a clean [b]Pokémon Manager[/b] window next to your Pokémon Chest, so you can look after dozens of Pokémon Huts and Barns without walking to each one. It can also send what your Pokémon carry straight into the chests you choose, and it keeps big farms running smoothly.

It does [b]not[/b] change or redistribute Pelipper Town. Every assign, unassign, chore, breeding and delivery change goes through Pelipper Town's own commands, so all of its rules still apply (blocked doors, water-only Pokémon, one resident per hut, owner checks). If something is refused, you get a readable reason instead of a silent failure.

[size=5][b][color=#e8a317]Installation instructions[/color][/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install [b]SMAPI 4.x[/b] and [b]Pelipper Town 1.2.7 or newer[/b] (with the mods it requires, such as SpaceCore).[/*]
[*]Download this mod and unzip it.[/*]
[*]Copy the folder [b]pelipper_expander_pokemanager[/b] into [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b].[/*]
[*]Start the game through SMAPI. The SMAPI log should say that Pelipper Town was detected and that the bridge was validated.[/*]
[*]Stand within 3 tiles of a [b]Pokémon Chest[/b] and press [b]K[/b] (rebindable) to open the Manager.[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b][color=#e8a317]Main features[/color][/b][/size]

[size=4][b]Evolve tab[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Lists every boxed Pokémon that Pelipper Town would let evolve, with avatars for the Pokémon and its evolution target(s).[/*]
[*]Evolve one, or evolve all ready Pokémon one after another. Pelipper Town's own evolution dialogue is used, so route choices and animations stay intact.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Huts tab[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Overview:[/b] every Pokémon Hut inside the managed area, with position, distance, resident, HP and energy bars, chore chips and item delivery.[/*]
[*][b]Detail panel:[/b] click a hut to toggle each chore and to switch item delivery between the chest and you. Chores a Pokémon cannot do are marked with a red X.[/*]
[*][b]Search, filter, sort:[/b] search by name, species or x,y. Filter by Empty / Occupied, delivery target and chores ("Has all": a Pokémon must be able to do [i]all[/i] the chosen chores). Sort by position, distance, name, level or energy.[/*]
[*][b]Assign:[/b] a large picker with accent-insensitive search, sorting, minimum level, chore filter and a picture of every Pokémon. Pokémon that cannot be placed are dimmed, with the reason.[/*]
[*][b]Unassign / Unassign all:[/b] unassign all asks for confirmation.[/*]
[*][b]Template and sync:[/b] set a hut as template, then sync its chores, delivery and chests to all huts or only the ticked ones.[/*]
[*][b]Safe batch actions:[/b] they never stop at the first problem and report "N ok, M failed (most common reason)".[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Quick assign in 3 steps[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Tick the empty huts you want to fill, then press [b]Quick assign[/b]. A green box next to the button shows it is on.[/*]
[*]Choose the chores in the [b]Has all[/b] filter. While Quick assign is on, this filter only picks the Pokémon and does not hide any huts.[/*]
[*]Press the button again. Free Pokémon that can do every chosen chore fill the ticked huts, and the list switches to [b]All[/b] so you can see who was placed.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Barns tab (new)[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Overview:[/b] each barn shows its tile, distance, pairs used (for example 2/4), slots used and its drops as short chips. A bigger barn holds more pairs: 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 slots give 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 pairs.[/*]
[*][b]Open a barn:[/b] click its row to see its pair slots. Each slot shows the two Pokémon with a blue male or pink female symbol after the name and drop chip (hover the symbol for the role), and has [i]Assign[/i], [i]Breed on/off[/i] and [i]Unassign[/i]. The Breed button on the barn row switches every pair of that barn at once.[/*]
[*][b]Assign a pair:[/b] pick the first parent, then the second. The picker dims Pokémon that cannot breed together and tells you why (same Pokémon, no species data, gender, no offspring, already busy).[/*]
[*][b]Name a barn:[/b] press [i]Name[/i] on its row, type up to 24 characters, press OK. [i]Clear name[/i] removes it. Names are searchable.[/*]
[*][b]Drops filter:[/b] choose what you want to farm (M, FQ...) and only the barns that give it stay in the list.[/*]
[*][b]Search and Show:[/b] search by name, tile, Pokémon or drop. Show All / Empty / Occupied.[/*]
[*][b]Batch buttons:[/b] Select all, Clear selection, Breed on / off for the ticked barns, Unassign all (asks twice).[/*]
[*][b]Unassign refused?[/b] A pair that still holds an egg cannot be released. Collect the egg and try again. The status line says so.[/*]
[*][b]Barn animations switch:[/b] one button next to the performance preset, for people who do not need the barn pets moving.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Quick pair in 3 steps[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Tick the barns you want to fill, then press [b]Quick pair[/b]. A green box next to the button shows it is on, and the list is not filtered.[/*]
[*]Choose the goods in the [b]Drops[/b] chips. "Both parents" decides whether both Pokémon or only one has to drop them.[/*]
[*]Press the button again. Free compatible Pokémon fill every free pair slot of the ticked barns. The box switches off by itself when nothing is left to fill.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Target chests: items go where you want them[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Open the picker:[/b] select a hut and press [b]Chest...[/b], or click the chest chip on its row. It lists the vanilla chests around the hut (Chest, Stone Chest, Big Chest, Big Stone Chest).[/*]
[*][b]Choose:[/b] click rows to pick several chests, [b]Name[/b] to name a chest (also available inside the game's own chest menu), [b]Apply[/b] to save, [b]No chest[/b] to return to Pelipper Town's original behaviour.[/*]
[*][b]Each row shows:[/b] name, type, paint colour, slots used and how many huts use that chest.[/*]
[*][b]Order of delivery:[/b] an item goes first to a chest that already holds it, so stacks grow and chests stay sorted, then to the other chosen chests in the order you picked them.[/*]
[*][b]Queue:[/b] huts with 6+ items join a queue. One batch every 3 seconds empties up to 8 huts. Items waiting for a delivery to you are never touched. All of this is adjustable.[/*]
[*][b]Range:[/b] a chest must be within [font=Courier New]RouteMaxDistanceTiles[/font] (default 100) of its hut when both are in the same place. A chest in another loaded location, such as a shed, has no distance limit.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Radius up to 100 tiles[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]The managed area is a radius around the chest: [b]5 = 11x11[/b] tiles, [b]100 = 201x201[/b] tiles.[/*]
[*]Use the -10 / -1 / +1 / +10 buttons or type a number and press Enter.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Performance and lag guard[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Low / Normal preset:[/b] one button. Low turns off hut animations, barn animations, effects, toy play, strolls and barn markers. Each one also has its own switch.[/*]
[*][b]Teleport on trips:[/b] work trips, returning home and chest trips can teleport instead of walking ([font=Courier New]HutTeleport[/font], from [font=Courier New]HutTeleportMinTiles[/font] tiles). Idle strolls still walk.[/*]
[*][b]Frame budget:[/b] [font=Courier New]HutFrameBudgetMs[/font] (2.5 ms) caps the hut update per frame. Off-screen workers update every [font=Courier New]HutOffscreenSliceTicks[/font] ticks (4).[/*]
[*][b]Return-loop guard and search smoothing:[/b] still on from 0.5.5. A blocked Pokémon waits longer between searches and is sent home after a few seconds, and "find work" and "stroll" searches share one search per tick.[/*]
[*][b]Search budget in real time:[/b] [font=Courier New]HutSearchMsPerSec[/font] (0 = off) and [font=Courier New]MountedSearchMsPerSec[/font] (40) limit how many milliseconds per second the path searches may use.[/*]
[*][b]Riding:[/b] [font=Courier New]MountedThrottle[/font] postpones the chest batch and slices workers while you ride.[/*]
[*][b]Spike log:[/b] [font=Courier New]SpikeLogMs[/font] (40) writes every slow update to the SMAPI log with what ran in it (0 = off).[/*]
[*]Works by patching a few private Pelipper Town methods at run time. Nothing is copied, and any error inside the guard falls back to the original behaviour.[/*]
[*]Tip: when a Pokémon is sent home, the SMAPI log names the tile. If it is the same tile again and again (a narrow gap, a pond edge, a crowded doorway), widening that spot removes the cause.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Vietnamese language option[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Turn on [b]Vietnamese[/b] in the settings to show the whole Manager in Vietnamese.[/*]
[*]A bundled pixel font (VT323) makes sure every Vietnamese letter displays correctly. Pokémon names and nicknames are not translated, and Lv / HP / id stay as they are.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Settings[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Edit [b]config.json[/b], use [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] (optional), or use the SMAPI console: [font=Courier New]pe_config[/font], [font=Courier New]pe_set <Key> <Value>[/font], [font=Courier New]pe_reset[/font], [font=Courier New]pe_range <radius>[/font].[/*]
[*]Values are clamped to safe limits and apply immediately, no restart needed.[/*]
[*][b]Chests:[/b] [font=Courier New]EnableRouting[/font], [font=Courier New]RouteMinItems[/font] (6), [font=Courier New]RouteIntervalTicks[/font] (180), [font=Courier New]RouteMaxHutsPerBatch[/font] (8), [font=Courier New]RouteMaxDistanceTiles[/font] (100).[/*]
[*][b]Lag guard:[/b] [font=Courier New]FixHutReturnLoop[/font] (true), [font=Courier New]SmoothHutSearches[/font] (true), [font=Courier New]HutSearchesPerTick[/font] (1), [font=Courier New]HutUnstickAfterRetries[/font] (4, 0 = never send a blocked Pokémon home).[/*]
[*][b]Barns:[/b] [font=Courier New]BarnQuickPairRequireBoth[/font] (true), [font=Courier New]BarnDefaultBreeding[/font] (true), [font=Courier New]BarnNames[/font] (set from the Barns tab).[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Console commands (for looking, not needed for the fixes)[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][font=Courier New]pe_huts[/font]: how many huts were found in range.[/*]
[*][font=Courier New]pe_stall[/font]: what the lag guard did (go-home searches let through and held back, Pokémon sent home, searches pushed to a later tick).[/*]
[*][font=Courier New]pe_route[/font]: how many huts carry items, which are held back and why, with the chest's used/total slots.[/*]

[*]The [font=Courier New]searches pushed to a later tick[/font] counter in [font=Courier New]pe_stall[/font] grows very fast on a big farm. That is normal, no search is lost.[/*]
